name: Revit_GFA_Calculator
provenance: Reviewed and anonymized Demo snapshot of every reusable Revit GFA rule explicitly enumerated in product specification Issue #1. The original personal-skill file was not present in the repository and is not claimed as a byte-for-byte source.
applicability: Revit 2026 demo planning for Area Scheme, Area Plan, boundary-source comparison, Area placement, tags and schedule QA. Project policy still requires user confirmation.
rules: Area Plans do not create Area Boundary lines automatically; boundary generation is a separate operation.
Use exact Revit curve loops and topology to validate a boundary; never substitute a bounding box for a footprint.
Walls, floors, roofs and existing Area Boundary lines are candidate evidence rather than universally authoritative sources.
A roof-level structural floor can be stronger coverage evidence than a floor hosted on the target level.
Keep geometric coverage evidence separate from regulatory, classification and GFA-factor policy decisions.
Uncovered corridors, balconies and other special regions require project confirmation rather than a universal fixed factor.
A screenshot is supporting evidence only and must be checked against structured Revit geometry.
Place Areas and tags at points verified to be inside a valid closed circuit; do not use a bounding-box center for a complex region.
Check Area Boundary breaks, self-intersections, illegal short curves, zero-area circuits and duplicate Areas as blocking QA.
Review hidden as well as visible schedule grouping fields, and disable itemized rows when same-level same-classification Areas must aggregate.
Reuse an existing Color Scheme and a user-confirmed Area Tag type; do not silently replace project graphics.
A first use of a classification or GFA factor remains a proposal until the user confirms it for the current project.
Priority order is current user instruction, manually locked result, confirmed project rule, prior AI result, then new AI inference.
Treat user edits as higher-priority external changes and do not silently overwrite a locked region.
A committed Revit transaction is not proof of success; read back model elements and verify the resulting view or schedule.
Do not automatically save the RVT after analysis, draft generation, QA or user confirmation.
